# Civic-hours certificate

## Status
**Deferred** — blocked on
[`personhood-verification`](./personhood-verification.md). Do not ship
certification until that resolves.

## Summary
Let a contributor generate a printable certificate attesting the volunteer hours
they logged via the quest board — usable for court-ordered community service,
resume/volunteer records, or hours-for-tickets programs. Original design and
rationale: SPEC §4 and
[`note-donor-bounties`](../../DESIGN_NOTES_2026-05-19_donor_bounties_and_claim_reporting.md).

## Why it's deferred (not rejected)
The original design deliberately stored **no** real-name binding and ran **no**
promotion/approval workflow, because it leaned entirely on one external fact:
wiki accounts were issued only after in-person admin verification, so every
claim was implicitly by a vouched-for human. The move to
[`local-auth`](../decisions/0001-local-auth.md) **removed that fact.** Every
assumption in the certificate design that depended on it is now unsupported.

The idea is still good — makerspaces genuinely want this. It is parked until a
personhood signal exists to rebuild the chain on.

## To revive
1. Land a [`personhood-verification`](./personhood-verification.md) approach.
2. Re-derive the certificate's trust language from that signal (not from wiki
   account policy).
3. Re-check the Sybil and credential-sharing mitigations against

# Design-docs information architecture

How design knowledge is organized in this repo so that **what's true now**,
**what we've committed to build**, and **what we might (or decided not to) do**
each have a distinct home — readable by humans and LLMs, and renderable as a
graph by an external app.

This exists because prose drifts. An idea that gets dropped leaves no trace
except an old assertion it now contradicts (see the multi-character and
civic-hours churn in the git history). The fix: **status is a first-class
field, and rejected/deferred ideas are kept, not deleted.**

---

## The model: every doc is a typed node in a graph

One Markdown file = one **node**. Its YAML frontmatter is the machine-readable
contract; the body is for humans/LLMs. Relationships between docs are **typed
edges** declared in frontmatter. `scripts/build_docs_index.py` walks every
doc's frontmatter and emits [`index.json`](./index.json) — a `{nodes, edges}`
graph that an LLM can read without opening every file, and that a viewer
(Cytoscape / D3, or Obsidian via wikilinks) can draw. Each node also carries a
`body` (an inline preview of the doc's prose) and a `source` link (the
originating document on GitHub, with a section anchor inferred from the `reason`
— e.g. `SPEC §3` → `#3-economy-yaml`), so both views can lead from a node into
its full description and the document it came from.

Four things do

… *(truncated — open the source document for the full text)*

# Local accounts instead of wiki SSO

## Status
Shipped — migration `0008_password_hash`, `app/local_auth.py`, `app/auth.py`,
routes `/register` `/login` `/logout` `/me/password`.

## Context
The Noisebridge Quest Board originally authenticated by proxying credentials to
the Noisebridge MediaWiki (`action=login` against `noisebridge.net/api.php`,
same pattern as nbarchive). The Actropolis rebrand generalized the product
across multiple makerspaces, where "the NB wiki" is not a shared identity
provider.

## Decision
Accounts are **local**: a username + an Argon2id password hash stored in
`users.password_hash`. Self-serve `/register` and `/login`; password change at
`/me/password`; admin bootstrap/reset via `scripts.set_password`. The wiki login
proxy and `wiki_api.py` were removed.

## Rejected alternatives
- **Keep wiki SSO.** Ties every makerspace to NB's wiki; wrong for a multi-space
  product.
- **MediaWiki OAuth.** The NB wiki has no OAuth extension installed, and it
  carries the same single-provider coupling.

## Consequences
- Signup is self-serve, which **broke the in-person personhood guarantee** that
  wiki accounts used to provide. That guarantee underpinned the civic-hours
  certificate — see [`civic-hours-cert`](../proposals/civic-hours-cert.md) and
  [`personhood-verification`](../proposals/personhood-verification.md).
- `users.wiki_username` was renamed to `usern

nodes.title: No runtime LLM quest generation
nodes.body:
# No runtime LLM quest generation

## Status
Accepted (2026-05-09). Reflected in the shipped quest pool: 348 seeds ingested
once, none generated live.

## Context
An early demo idea had NPC quest-givers call Ollama at runtime to generate fresh
quests for color. That couples the request path to a local model's latency and
output quality, and makes the live world non-deterministic and hard to review.

## Decision
**No LLM calls at runtime.** The LLM is used only **offline, once**, during data
prep — `curate_discord.py` cleans mined Discord messages and `tag_skills.py`
assigns skills. The live `quests` table is seeded from that fixed, human-review-
able pool (`data/quest_templates/discord_tagged.yaml`). NPCs, when the simulator
lands, draw from the seed pool plus hand-curated templates.

## Consequences
- The data pipeline (`mine → curate → tag → ingest`) is repeatable but not part
  of the runtime.
- Any future "fresh quests" feature is a separate proposal, not an implicit
  runtime behavior.

# Design Notes — Donor Bounties + Claim Reporting

**Date:** 2026-05-19
**Status:** Merged into SPEC.md 2026-05-19 (data model, mechanics, API surface, civic-hours certificate). This doc retained as the rationale / why-we-did-what record.
**Origin:** Discord thread — Project Forum › *NoiseQuest: Task Gamification + Catalogue System* — economics sub-discussion, 2026-05-19 ~17:51–19:13 UTC. Daniel (Web) proposed a donation-bounty mechanic; this doc captures the design that emerged from talking it through. The civic-hours layer (§8) was added later the same day after surfacing the in-progress SF City parking-ticket conversation.

---

## 1. What this adds to v1

Two new layers on top of the existing quest model:

1. **Donor bounties** — real-dollar gifts to NB, conditional on a quest being completed. The volunteer is never paid; the bounty goes to NB.
2. **Claim reporting** — per-claimer self-reported time, notes, photo, and done-state at claim-completion time.

Neither requires a redesign of the existing schema. Both attach cleanly to existing tables.

---

## 2. Donor bounties — the model

### What it is

A donor pledges $X to Noisebridge **conditional** on quest Y being completed. When a party claims and marks the quest done, NB collects the gift. The volunteer receives XP (existing mechanic), recognition, and the legible fact that their labor unlocked a real-dollar donation —

# One profile per account (both modes)

## Status
Shipped — `create_default_profile` runs at signup; there is no
`/me/characters/new`, `/activate`, or `/delete` flow. `/me/characters` is the
single "YOUR PROFILE" editor.

## Context
The original demo design (see DEMO.md history) let a player create **up to 4
characters** per account and watch them auto-play, with the "real" tool
constraining this to 1:1 via config. Carrying two identity cardinalities doubled
the surface area of every character-scoped feature (claims, XP ledger, active
selection, UI).

## Decision
**One profile per account, in both the demo and the real tool.** The profile is
a single `characters` row created at signup and pointed to by
`users.active_character_id`. Identity splits into three names on the account:
`username` (login, fixed), a freely-changeable **visible name**, and a private
`real_name` + `show_real_name` toggle (migrations `0010`, `0011`).

## Rejected alternatives
- **Up to 4 characters in the demo (multi-character).** Dropped — the extra
  cardinality wasn't worth the complexity, and a single profile still delivers
  the Progress-Quest auto-play feel.

## Consequences
- "Character" and "profile" are now the same single per-account row; docs use
  "profile."
- The multi-character UI affordances (`MAKE ACTIVE`, the `☠` retire button,
  empty slots, `demo.max_characters_per_user`) are retired.

# Actropolis

A quest board for the Actropolis network of makerspaces — a Progress-Quest-style
task board built so a future "real" version can be inherited from the same
codebase without rewriting.

**Live:** <https://quests.actropolis.org/>

---

## What changed (Oct 2026)

Formerly the "Noisebridge Quest Board." Now rebranded **Actropolis** and generalized
to span multiple makerspaces:

- **Independent accounts.** Auth no longer proxies to the Noisebridge wiki. Accounts
  are local (username + Argon2id password), created via `/register`, changed via the
  profile panel (`/me/password`). Admin bootstrap/reset: `python -m scripts.set_password <user>`.
- **Spaces (makerspaces).** A `spaces` table models member sites (Noisebridge, Sequoia
  Fabrica, OpenCircuit SF, Omni Commons). Users pick a **primary makerspace** on their
  profile; quests can be scoped to a space (shown on cards + detail, filterable in browse).
- **Hosting.** Served at `quests.actropolis.org` (Apache reverse-proxy → uvicorn :8080 on
  zephyr). Admin allow-list lives at `/home/nthmost/.questboard-economy.yaml` (outside the
  repo, pointed to by an `ECONOMY_YAML_PATH` systemd drop-in).

> **⚠ Civic-hours caveat.** SPEC §1 / §4 and the DESIGN_NOTES civic-hours certificate
> depended on the fact that *wiki accounts were issued only after in-person admin
> verification* — making `wiki_username` ≈ a verified human.

nodes.title: Personhood verification for local accounts
nodes.body:
# Personhood verification for local accounts

## Status
Exploring. This is the **blocker** for anything that certifies a real human's
contribution — most directly the civic-hours certificate.

## Context
When auth proxied to the NB wiki, a `username` was effectively 1:1 with a
vouched-for human, because wiki accounts were issued only after in-person admin
verification. The move to [`local-auth`](../decisions/0001-local-auth.md) made
signup self-serve and **removed that guarantee**. Nothing in the system now
attests that an account is a distinct real person.

## The question
How do we re-establish a "this account is a verified human" signal strong enough
to back civic-hours / volunteer-credit certification, without storing PII at
rest?

## Candidate approaches (unscored)
- **Admin approval of accounts** — a lightweight re-creation of the old gate; an
  admin marks an account verified. Centralizes work on admins.
- **Per-space vouching** — an existing verified member of a makerspace vouches
  for a new account in that space. Scales better; needs a vouch model and
  abuse handling.
- **Tiered trust** — unverified accounts can play; only verified accounts can
  generate a certifiable record. Decouples "play" from "certify."

## Downstream
Resolving this unblocks [`civic-hours-cert`](./civic-hours-cert.md).

# Progress-Quest simulator

## Status
Accepted, **not yet built** — the largest remaining slice of the demo. Design
lives in DEMO.md §6; this node tracks it as a unit of work.

## Summary
An async tick loop (one real second per tick, 30× sim speedup) that advances
`sim_state`, fires NPC quest posts, runs profile auto-claim/auto-complete to
maturity, writes append-only `simulation_events`, and drives a live SSE feed at
`/api/v1/feed/stream`.

## What it unblocks (currently stubbed because the sim doesn't run)
- Live SSE activity feed (the front page renders real recent activity today via
  `_real_feed`, but not a live stream).
- The active profile's "current task" panel (always `RESTING` today).
- NPC quest-giver rows (`npc_quest_givers` table exists, no rows).
- An admin reset endpoint to wipe simulation state.

## Open questions
- Reset cadence (weekly vs admin-on-demand).
- NPC count / personas per guild.
- Whether to run the sim at all on the Noisebridge ("real board") instance — per
  config it should not seed NPCs or run a sim clock.

# Quest Board — UI Reference

> **Orientation:** Front-end visual reference — palette, panel system,
> component vocabulary, page-by-page layout. Snapshot of the live state at
> <https://quests.actropolis.org/> (visual register as of 2026-05-09; pages,
> auth, and routes reconciled to the shipped code 2026-10-26). Living document;
> update when the visual register or component vocabulary changes.
> If you're brand new, start with [README.md](./README.md).

## 1. Stack & file layout

- **Server-rendered Jinja2 templates**, no SPA. FastAPI returns full pages.
- **htmx + SSE** anticipated for live-update surfaces (activity feed, character sheet) once the simulator lands. Not used yet.
- **Static CSS only** at `app/static/css/nes.css`. No JS framework, no preprocessor.
- Cache-buster: every page link to the CSS includes `?v=<mtime>`, computed once at app startup from the file's mtime. Browsers re-fetch automatically when the CSS changes — no hard-reload needed.

```
app/
├── templates/
│   ├── base.html               # html shell + asset_v cache buster + footer
│   ├── index.html              # /
│   ├── login.html              # /login
│   ├── register.html           # /register
│   ├── me_characters.html      # /me/characters ("YOUR PROFILE")
│   ├── quest_create.html       # /quests/new
│   ├── admin_layout.html       # admin shell

nodes.title: Embeddable user-page badges
nodes.body:
# Embeddable user-page badges

## Status
Proposed, not built. SPEC §ext mentions it; this node tracks the decision.

## Summary
An endpoint set any external page (a personal site, a makerspace wiki user-page)
can embed to render an account's quest-board status — level, XP, quest count,
recent activity — as SVG / JSON / HTML.

## Open question — path naming
The original sketch used `/api/v1/users/by-wiki/{username}/badge.{svg,json,html}`.
Now that accounts are local rather than wiki-derived
([`local-auth`](../decisions/0001-local-auth.md)), the `by-wiki` segment is
misleading. Proposed rename: `/api/v1/users/by-username/{username}/badge.*`.
Decide before implementing, since it's a public URL contract.

## Notes
- Cache aggressively at the reverse proxy (the DEPLOYMENT template already sketches
  a `proxy_cache_valid` block for the badge path).
- Server-rendered SVG with a cached variant is the "badge fetcher" persona's need.
